captions.caption: Title card introducing Corporal Benjamin Pitre at Camp Pendleton, California, demonstrating Combat Lifesavers Course skills.
Information about the unit and videographer is displayed on a black background.
The intro text concludes with a mention of the corporal's recent training.
A brief black screen transitions between the intro text and the demonstration.
Corporal Pitre sits on the ground in military fatigues, holding a black SAM splint.
He holds the flexible black splint with both hands, ready to demonstrate its use.
The corporal explains the splint's application for fractured arms and legs.
He manipulates the splint to show its flat, flexible form.
Corporal Pitre looks at the camera while describing how the splint supports injuries.
He continues to sit cross-legged on the grass near a concrete path.
The corporal gestures with the splint as he details the medical procedure.
He starts to demonstrate the physical properties of the splint material.
He holds the long splint vertically to show its length relative to his body.
Corporal Pitre continues his explanation while handling the medical equipment.
He prepares to fold the splint to show a specific configuration.
The corporal begins folding the black splint in half crosswise.
He aligns the ends of the folded splint to create a double layer.
He presses the two halves of the splint together.
Corporal Pitre demonstrates the size of the folded splint against his leg.
He unfolds the splint back to its full length.
He begins a new folding technique, bending the splint lengthwise.
The corporal folds the long edges of the splint towards each other.
He creases the center of the splint to create a structural "V" shape.
He places the shaped splint against his left forearm to check the fit.
Corporal Pitre adjusts the splint's position near his wrist.
He explains the importance of molding the splint to the specific limb.
He starts using his fingers to further shape the material around his wrist.
The corporal continues molding the splint with concentrated hand movements.
He ensures the splint follows the natural contour of his arm.
A close-up shot focuses on his hands bending the flexible black splint material.
He uses his thumbs to create a curve in the splint's structural fold.
The corporal carefully shapes the end of the splint to fit a hand.
He continues to manipulate the material, demonstrating its moldability.
His hands move along the length of the splint, refining its shape.
He applies pressure to create a rigid support structure.
The corporal checks the rigidity of the molded splint.
He makes a final adjustment to the curve near the wrist area.
He finishes the molding process, showing the completed shape in close-up.
The corporal holds the shaped splint, ready for application.
The camera pans back to show Corporal Pitre sitting with the molded splint.
He places the molded splint onto his left forearm and wrist.
The corporal demonstrates the significant support the splint provides.
He holds his splinted arm up to show how it immobilizes the joint.
He explains that the splint prevents any movement of the fracture site.
He keeps his left arm steady while speaking to the camera.
Corporal Pitre uses his right hand to point out features of the splint.
He continues to discuss the effectiveness of the immobilization technique.
He looks down at his arm to ensure the splint is properly placed.
He adjusts the splint's alignment on his forearm.
The corporal prepares for the next step in securing the medical device.
He reaches down to pick up a roll of tan elastic bandage from the ground.
He holds the bandage roll, ready to wrap it over the splint.
Corporal Pitre explains that the bandage will keep the splint from moving.
He begins to unroll the end of the tan bandage.
He positions the start of the bandage wrap near his wrist.
He starts the first wrap of the elastic bandage around the splint.
The corporal expertly wraps the bandage, securing the splint to his arm.
He continues the wrapping motion, moving up his forearm.
He ensures the bandage is applied with even tension.
Corporal Pitre continues to wrap the bandage while looking at other supplies on the ground.
